subject: System Design
title: Why Systems Will Always Fail
description: A quick win: understand Why Systems Will Always Fail.

hook.text: Despite decades of engineering, outages keep happening. AWS, Google, Facebook — nobody is immune.

buildup.text: Complex systems have emergent behaviors that no single person fully understands.

discovery.text: Normal Accident Theory says failures in tightly coupled, complex systems are inevitable, not exceptional.

twist.text: The goal isn't to prevent all failures — it's to detect them fast, limit their blast radius, and recover quickly.

climax.text: The best teams don't aim for zero failures. They aim for fast detection, small blast radius, and quick recovery.

punchline.text: Failures are inevitable — recovery speed is the real metric.

quiz.question: What does Normal Accident Theory say?
options: Failures in complex tightly coupled systems are inevitable
